same_choices: Bookmark/ribbon is the icon and the governing metaphor (ink-filled bookmark vs. ribbon tucked into a slot)
A 'Saved' text pill slides in beside the button as the confirmation, positioned next to the control rather than over it
Dark surface (near-black slate / deep navy) with a single warm accent color reserved exclusively for the saved state
Saved rest state adds a non-color legibility cue on top of fill so state does not depend on color memory
Click-triggered, optimistic commit that starts immediately and reconciles with the server, reverting (ink drains / flip settles back) on failure
An explicit in-flight pending cue distinct from both idle and saved
Dark navy/slate surface with a near-identical amber accent for the saved state
A short text word animates in on confirm ('Saved' / 'Moored')
A dedicated at-rest, motion-independent state marker for accessibility ('Saved' label vs. corner badge)
Motion primitive is a flip about the vertical axis that reveals a filled committed face (fold/origami scaleX flip vs. rotateY card flip) — a user experiences both as the button turning over
Dark deep-navy surface with a single warm accent reserved exclusively for the saved state

enumeration_overlap: underline tick / accent underline saved cue (01, 02)
confirmation beside the button / trailing toast (02, 03)
notes: All three fully realize their tables — every committed option is identifiable from the body without the table. Real convergence is in the shared option pools (flip, morph, hover-x, audio) and in 01/03's near-identical click+optimistic+pending+dark-amber skeleton.
